title: N-Acetylcysteine (NAC) in Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis (PSC)
official: A Proof-of-Principle Pilot Study of N-Acetylcysteine (NAC) Monotherapy to Assess Biochemical Changes in Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis (PSC)
summary:
Primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC) is a chronic disease that causes inflammation and scarring of the bile ducts and can lead to progressive liver damage. There are currently no approved medications that have been shown to improve long-term outcomes in patients with PSC.

The purpose of this pilot study is to evaluate whether N-acetylcysteine (NAC), a medication that helps the body produce an antioxidant called glutathione, may improve liver blood tests in people with PSC.

This is a single-center, open-label study involving approximately 15 adults with PSC. All participants will receive oral NAC at a dose of 1,200 mg per day for the first 12 weeks. At Week 12, the dose will either remain the same or increase to 1,800 mg per day, depending on changes in a liver blood test called alkaline phosphatase (ALP).

Participants will continue treatment through Week 16. Those with a substantial improvement in ALP may be eligible to continue treatment through Week 20.

Researchers will evaluate changes in liver blood tests, treatment safety, side effects, and medication adherence. Additional blood tests may help researchers better understand how NAC affects liver injury.

This study is intended to provide preliminary information about the potential benefits and safety of NAC in PSC. It is not designed to establish whether NAC is an effective treatment for PSC.
criteria:
\*\*Inclusion Criteria:\*\*

* Adults aged 18 to 70 years.
* Diagnosis of primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC) for at least 6 months, confirmed by characteristic cholangiographic findings, without evidence of secondary sclerosing cholangitis.
* Serum alkaline phosphatase (ALP) greater than 1.33 times the upper limit of normal at screening.
* Platelet count greater than 150,000/mm³, serum albumin greater than 3.3 g/dL, and serum creatinine below the upper limit of normal.
* For participants receiving ursodeoxycholic acid (UDCA), a stable dose for at least 3 months before screening. Participants not receiving UDCA must have been off UDCA for at least 3 months.
* For participants receiving mesalamine, sulfasalazine, immunomodulators, or biologic medications for inflammatory bowel disease, a stable dose for at least 4-8 weeks before enrollment, with no planned treatment changes during the study.
* For participants receiving oral corticosteroids, a daily dose not exceeding 20 mg of prednisone or 6 mg of budesonide at enrollment.
* Willingness and ability to provide informed consent and comply with study visits, medication administration, and laboratory testing.
* No concurrent enrollment in another interventional PSC trial.

\*\*Exclusion Criteria:\*\*

* Pregnancy or breastfeeding.
* Known hypersensitivity to N-acetylcysteine (NAC) or any component of the study capsules.
* Alanine aminotransferase (ALT) greater than 10 times the upper limit of normal, total bilirubin greater than 2 times the upper limit of normal (except in participants with Gilbert syndrome), or international normalized ratio (INR) greater than 1.2.
* Decompensated cirrhosis, including ascites, hepatic encephalopathy, or variceal bleeding.
* Small-duct primary sclerosing cholangitis.
* Other causes of liver disease, including secondary sclerosing cholangitis, viral liver disease, alcohol-related liver disease, or other autoimmune liver diseases, including positive antimitochondrial antibodies. Participants with nonalcoholic fatty liver disease may be eligible if there is no evidence of nonalcoholic steatohepatitis.
* History of liver transplantation, hepatocellular carcinoma, or cholangiocarcinoma.
* Ascending cholangitis within 90 days before enrollment.
* Severe ulcerative colitis flare requiring intravenous corticosteroids within 3 weeks before enrollment, or an anticipated change to a new inflammatory bowel disease medication within 3 months.
* Concurrent participation in another therapeutic clinical trial.
* Any laboratory abnormality or medical condition that, in the investigator's judgment, could compromise participant safety or interfere with the evaluation of study outcomes.
* Current regular use of an NAC-containing supplement outside the study.
